packageRules.description: Everything that automerges (except noctalia-greeter, next rule) goes into ONE weekly PR: one full image build per week instead of one per dependency, and no rebase-and-rebuild cascade when one of many PRs merges. The Monday release ships it

What features build from source (each feature's build.sh: noctalia-greeter, shimmy) gets a PR of its own per dependency, automerged the same way, instead of joining the weekly one: a release that needs a build change, such as a new build dependency, would otherwise hold every other update in the weekly PR. Costs one more image build in the weeks one moves
A crates.io pin (features/llm/build.sh) is an exact version: Renovate's default cargo versioning would read 2.6.4 as the range ^2.6.4 and never propose an update

Every action is pinned to a commit for an exact version tag, so a digest update of one means that tag was moved to a different commit, which is what a hijacked action looks like (tj-actions/changed-files, 2025). Never automerged, never mixed into the weekly PR (one non-automerge update would hold the whole group), opened at once

Automerged updates wait 3 days after their release, so a broken or pulled release is usually gone before it is merged. Only for datasources that report release times: without one (e.g. the chunkah digest on quay.io) Renovate would hold the update forever

Claude Code (devtools/flatpak/build.sh, devtools/Containerfile) follows Anthropic's stable channel, the npm dist-tag 'stable': a release about a week old, skipping those with major regressions, instead of every daily one

The noctalia-greeter pin is a tag plus the commit that gets built (features/login/build.sh). A new commit for the same tag means upstream moved the tag: never automerged, never in the weekly PR, and opened at once (so after the 3-day rule above, which it lifts: a re-created tag is 0 days old)
Majors (and replacements) are never automerged: their own PR, CI runs on it, and it waits for the owner (assigned and asked for review) to merge it

Fedora base images are not managed as docker tags: the registries carry the next release (branched) and rawhide as plain numbers long before they are released, so a docker lookup would propose rawhide. The 'fedora' custom manager below follows released Fedora versions instead
The move to the next Fedora release: every pin in one PR, opened as soon as endoflife.date lists the release (i.e. once it is out, not on the weekend after), never automerged

customManagers.description: Fedora release the images are built on: the base image tags (Containerfiles, Justfile, the scanner container in scan.sh) and the release named in the README
Versions in workflow files under a '# renovate: datasource=... depName=...' comment (cosign-release, tool versions)

The development tools and VS Code extensions in devtools/tools.txt and extensions.txt: the line under each '# renovate:' comment is 'name version asset checksum members license [source]'. A checksum of sha256:<hex> (releases that publish none) is the digest the github-release-attachments datasource bumps with the version; the #sha256:<hex> of a license URL is not matched and stays as it is

Versions under a '# renovate:' comment in the dev container's Containerfile (ARG lines) and in the Flatpak's and the features' build scripts (VAR=value lines); where a build pins a commit (noctalia-greeter), NAME_COMMIT on the next line is bumped together with the version
